7. A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed v0 and an angle 𝜃 above the horizontal. What is the speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?
A. 𝑣0.
B. 𝑣0 cos 𝜃.
C. 𝑣0 sin 𝜃.
D. 0.
datasource_item.generated_question_text:
Q7. A soccer ball is kicked with initial speed \(v_0\) at an angle \(\theta\) above the horizontal (ignore air resistance). What is the ball’s speed at its maximum height?
A. \(v_0\)
This is incorrect because the vertical component decreases to zero at the top, reducing the speed.
B. \(v_0 \cos\theta\)
This is correct because at maximum height the vertical velocity is zero, so the speed equals the constant horizontal component \(v_0 \cos\theta\).
C. \(v_0 \sin\theta\)
This is incorrect because \(v_0 \sin\theta\) is the initial vertical component, which becomes zero at the top.
D. 0
This is incorrect because only the vertical component is zero at the top; the horizontal component remains.

Q13. A 62 kg person on a frictionless skateboard is initially at rest. They catch a 2.0 kg medicine ball thrown horizontally at 8.0 m/s. After the catch, what is the person’s speed (with the ball)?
A. 0.26 m/s
This is correct because momentum conservation for an inelastic catch gives \(v_f = \frac{(2.0)(8.0)}{62+2.0} \approx 0.25\,\mathrm{m/s}\) (about 0.26 m/s).
B. 0.13 m/s
This typically comes from mistakenly dividing by only the person’s mass and then halving again.
C. 8.0 m/s
This ignores that the catcher is much more massive, so the shared final speed must be far smaller than the ball’s initial speed.
D. 4.0 m/s
This incorrectly averages speeds instead of conserving momentum for a perfectly inelastic collision.
